pr.title: Carry a repository inbox between peers through the relay
pr.head: 1640edf0263329f7c9684ee76dca20360f12614e

summary: Projector’s inbox normally lets an agent ask its own user for a decision or report an outcome. This change extends it to people who exchange public keys: an agent posts an item to a peer, the peer or their agents respond, and the asking agent receives each reply through the encrypted relay.

This middle stack layer adds the repository-wide inbox, transport, command handlers, and reply delivery. The preceding layer manages trusted peers; the following layer adds the panel, console, and skill integration. Incoming items, your sent copies, and replies remain separate entries so a peer’s response does not decide whether your agent needs more replies.

cards.title: What travels and what stays local
cards.html:
• Peer: another person whose public key you explicitly configured.
  • Relay: encrypted records carried by hidden Git refs in a shared repository.
  • Mirror: the local repository inbox, with stable references such as r1.
  • State record: closes, snoozes, and replied sessions encrypted to your own key and merged across your machines.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: The three earlier findings are fixed, including retrying a reply refused by the encrypted size check. One P2 remains in failure rollback: another session can replicate a provisional replied marker before its failed reply is released, and a later state merge restores that marker and blocks retry. Exact-head CI, the configured local gate, and all 361 focused Python tests passed.

groups.title: Store repository inbox entries and state
groups.kicker: The item contract and its local representation
intro: Each inbox item identifies its repository and sender. A sent copy records the intended peer, and a reply names the item it answers. The new store gives each local entry a stable r reference and merges state separately, so state arriving before an item can still apply when the item opens.

Agent replies should stay open and be limited to one reply per session. Closing and reopening belong to the asking side’s state; a peer can withdraw their own incoming item without silently closing the asker’s sent copy.

files.note: Defines the record validators, local mirror, state merge, posting and response operations, and reply wake lines.

checks.text: Replayed the malformed-record and synchronized same-session fixtures: malformed Unicode was rejected without blocking later items, and concurrent calls queued one reply.
Replayed the 13,000-byte quote response: the encrypted-size refusal now leaves a short retry able to send.

Rollback removes a failed session’s mark only from the local mirror. A temporary relay fixture interleaved another session’s successful reply before the failure; its sealed state carried both marks. A second machine’s state update restored the failed mark on the first machine and blocked retry. Pending reply reservations must not enter replicated state before queuing succeeds.

files.note: Parses repository references alongside session item references and resolves the repository used by inbox commands.

groups.title: Carry encrypted records between peers
groups.kicker: Validation, limits, and synchronization through the relay
intro: The relay fetches the recipient’s encrypted inbox refs, opens records only from the local key or configured peers, and checks repository identity and reply ownership before mirroring them. Per-peer limits keep a reply stream from consuming the allowance for new items.

Your machines exchange their own state records and merge concurrent updates. A reply wakes the original asking session only on its originating machine, while the item remains open; the event names its peer origin and authority limit.

files.note: Adds user and state namespaces, sender-aware opening, reply pairing, state merging, and mirror pruning. Malformed strings and timestamps are rejected before use; a record-level error backstop rejects one bad record and preserves progress.
Sets the default per-peer hourly limit.
Adds the positive user-level agent.peer_limit setting.
Includes configured peer relays in collection status even without a current key.
Allows queued peer reply events only while their mirrored reply still exists.
Exercises peer exchange, state merging, validation, limits, wake delivery, concurrent replies, encrypted-size rejection, and local queue-failure rollback.

checks.text: Ran the peer tests with the focused relay, inbox, watch, config, and permission tests: all 361 tests passed, including the new size-refusal and queue-failure cases.

files.note: Extends the relay fixture to three machines and adapts assertions to sender-aware opening and last-opened peer status.

groups.title: Post to peers and respond from the CLI
groups.kicker: Repository items join the existing inbox commands
intro: The CLI routes --to posts to configured peers and repository references such as r1 to the new store. Agent responses identify the registered session, while user actions remain explicit through --as. Showing peer content prints its authority notice before the body.
The permission rules allow agent replies and closes under standing instructions. Answers and other actions that decide an outcome retain their existing confirmation boundary.

files.note: Wires peer posting, reply and close commands, repository item routing, listing, and readable peer provenance.
Allows inbox reply and close while preserving confirmation for decisions.
Checks that reply and close are allowed and answer still asks.

groups.title: Document the inbox workflow and stack boundary
groups.kicker: Commands and decisions for people using the feature
intro: The CLI guide describes sending, answering, replying, snoozing, closing, and reopening peer items. The project plan records the implementation decisions that connect the three stack layers, including the need to land the panel and console integration before the whole flow ships.
